story.iWant: to orchestrate agentic workflows for complex analytical queries
story.soThat: questions requiring planning and multiple steps can be answered autonomously

tasks.task: Implement query complexity classifier (simple vs analytical)
Implement workflow planner with task decomposition and dependency graph
Implement workflow executor with agent routing and parallel/sequential execution
Implement workflow timeout and graceful degradation fallback
Create integration tests for complete workflow orchestration
Update MCP tool and orchestrator integration
Document workflow orchestration patterns and API

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Query complexity classifier distinguishes simple vs multi-step analytical queries (accuracy >90%)
Workflow planner decomposes complex queries into sub-tasks with dependencies (WorkflowPlan with AgentTask list)
Sub-tasks routed to appropriate specialized agents (retrieval, analysis, synthesis) with >90% accuracy
Agent outputs passed between agents as inputs to subsequent steps via AgentState model
Workflow execution completes in <30 seconds for typical analytical queries (NFR5); <5s p50, <15s p95
Example workflow tested: "Calculate YoY revenue growth and explain variance" with complete 5-task pipeline
Workflow success rate >80% on complex test queries (15+ queries from ground truth)
Failed workflows fall back gracefully to simpler retrieval (NFR17, NFR32) with timeout handling (NFR26)

package.name: strands
package.description: AWS Strands v1.15.0 - event-driven agent orchestration framework
package.purpose: @tool decorator for agent definitions, Agent class for orchestration
package.usage: from strands import tool, Agent; @tool decorator for planner, executor functions

package.name: pydantic
package.purpose: Pydantic models for QueryComplexity, AgentTask, WorkflowPlan, AgentResult, AnalyticalQueryRequest/Response
package.usage: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field; class QueryComplexity(str, Enum)

package.name: asyncio
package.purpose: Parallel task execution via asyncio.gather(), timeout handling via asyncio.wait_for()
package.usage: asyncio.gather() for parallel retrievals, asyncio.wait_for(agent_call, timeout=15s) for timeout

package.name: mistral-sdk
package.description: Mistral API client (for orchestration model if using Mistral Small)
package.purpose: LLM for query decomposition and task routing (tunable to Claude)

constraints.constraint: Query complexity classifier must use keyword matching (no ML required) for <50ms latency
Workflow planner maximum 8 tasks per decomposition (manageable complexity)
Task dependencies represented as DAG with no circular dependencies; validates before execution
Inter-agent data passing via AgentState model; all agent outputs must be JSON-serializable (Strands requirement)
Fallback to Epic 1 query_financial_documents() on any agent timeout/exception (graceful degradation)
Monolithic architecture: all agents run in single Python process, no external services added
Use shared logging pattern: logger.info("...", extra={...}) with task_id, agent_type, execution_time_ms
No custom wrappers or abstractions; use AWS Strands @tool decorator as-is

interface.name: classify_query_complexity(query: str) → QueryComplexity
interface.description: Classify incoming query as SIMPLE or ANALYTICAL based on keyword matching

interface.name: decompose_query(query: str, complexity: QueryComplexity) → WorkflowPlan
interface.signature: async def decompose_query(query: str, complexity: QueryComplexity) → WorkflowPlan: ...
interface.description: Break complex query into list of AgentTask objects with dependency graph

interface.name: execute_workflow(plan: WorkflowPlan) → List[AgentResult]
interface.description: Execute workflow plan: route tasks to agents, handle parallel/sequential execution, inter-agent data passing

interface.name: analyze_financial_question(request: AnalyticalQueryRequest) → str
interface.description: New MCP tool for analytical queries; routes to workflow orchestrator or falls back to basic retrieval

interface.name: AgentTask (model)
interface.signature: class AgentTask(BaseModel): task_id: str; agent_type: AgentType; instruction: str; depends_on: Optional[List[str]] = None

interface.name: WorkflowPlan (model)
interface.signature: class WorkflowPlan(BaseModel): query: str; complexity: QueryComplexity; tasks: List[AgentTask]; estimated_duration_ms: int
interface.description: Complete workflow execution plan with tasks and dependencies

interface.name: AgentResult (model)
interface.signature: class AgentResult(BaseModel): task_id: str; agent_type: AgentType; success: bool; result: Any; execution_time_ms: int; error: Optional[str] = None
interface.description: Result from single agent execution; propagated to subsequent agents via AgentState

tests.standards: Follow pytest patterns from Epic 1-2: unit tests in tests/unit/, integration tests in tests/integration/ with @pytest.mark.slow decorator. Use asyncio for async testing. Mock Strands orchestrator if needed; use real agents + Qdrant for integration tests. Target <1s for unit tests (no external dependencies), <60s for integration tests (real services). Measure execution timing (p50, p95) for performance validation.
tests.locations: tests/unit/agentic/test_planner.py (classifier, decomposition) tests/unit/agentic/test_workflow_executor.py (routing, parallel/sequential) tests/integration/test_workflow_orchestration.py (complete workflows) tests/fixtures/story_3_5_complex_queries.json (15+ test queries)
